Majorities of Americans say they are proud (79%) and grateful (86%) to be Americans, according to a new Cato poll. However, far fewer believe in American exceptionalism. 

Only about a third (34%) believe that the US “stands above all other countries in the world,” while 40% think the US is “one of the greatest countries in the world, along with some others”—14% said there are other countries better than the US.

posts.text:
Being an American is a significant part of most Americans’ identity, second only to their family, according to a new Cato poll. 

This suggests that American identity has the capacity to transcend racial, religious, and gender divisions and offer people something they have in common.

Learn more: ow.ly/iCqF50Zk41w

SCOTUS struck down the effort to limit birthright citizenship, holding that the 14th Amendment guarantees citizenship to nearly all children born on US soil. This will limit executive power and prevent a future president or Congress from undoing the rule, says Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry.

posts.text:
Reports that OpenAI discussed giving the federal government a 5% stake should concern anyone who wants the US to set the pace in AI, says Cato’s @DeHavenTad. Government ownership blurs the line between referee and market participants, creating political risk for developers, customers, and international partners. 
 
“Washington should strengthen US competitiveness through clear, neutral rules—not by taking equity in the companies it regulates.”
posts.summary: Opposes government equity stake in OpenAI, warns political risk
